alternatingChange.observation: Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. The broad middle-left branching group at 2500 clears to two small separated fragments by 3000. The diagonal central-right arrangement breaks into smaller upper and lower groups with larger open gaps. These are occupied-body changes, not just food or color changes.

seasonalChanges.observation: Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. Majority-fed band1 expands its small upper cluster into a wide dense upper branching mass, and its lower scattered bodies become a dense lower cluster. Minority-fed band0 loses the upper-left lattice and most lower-left bodies, leaving sparse middle-left fragments.

Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. Majority-fed band0 expands its sparse middle-left fragments into a broad branching group spanning the central-left region. Minority-fed band1 clears the large upper mass almost entirely, leaving an open upper region and smaller central and lower groups.

Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. Band0 clears most of its central-left branching group. Band1 also loses occupied structure: the broad diagonal central-right group contracts into separated smaller clusters. Both bands retreat overall; this does not show the required majority-band expansion.

sameAgeComparisons.observation: Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. Historical alternating has large upper-left and bottom-left lattices and small lower band1 clusters. The food-floor world has a compact upper-left lattice, a lower-left cluster and a distinct upper band1 group.

Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. Both worlds have sparse left-side bodies and substantial band1 structure. Historical alternating has denser lower band1 branching; the food-floor world has its largest mass in upper band1 with a smaller lower cluster.

Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. Historical alternating is sparse, with small separated bodies in both bands. The food-floor world retains a broad central-left group and diagonal central-right branching bodies.

Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. Historical alternating has tall upper band1 branching and a lower band1 network, plus several left groups. The food-floor world is sparser on the left and has separated central-right clusters. This is a descriptive difference, not general superiority.
